cases.title: Kusnap
cases.headline:
Making a marketplace
people can trust
cases.blurb: Kusnap made it easy to sign up and sell in seconds, and fraudsters used that. Of the many features I designed as Head of Design, two had a big impact on usage and transactions: seller verification and a new way to list products. Together they let buyers trust who they’re buying from and what they’re buying, without slowing honest sellers down.
story: A verification system that kept signing up fast
Kusnap launched with no verification at all, so anyone could list in seconds. Listings grew quickly, and so did fraud reports and calls from worried buyers and sellers.
I designed a verification system in two parts: one for individual buyers and sellers, one for business-owned stores. The aim was more trust without making onboarding slower.

blocks.v: Kusnap is a peer-to-peer marketplace for buying and selling across Nigeria, from brand-new to fairly used and second-hand items. It started with one simple goal: get people signed up and listing their products as fast as possible. That speed is the “snap” in Kusnap, and it worked in the early days.

Over time, fraudsters exploited it. They signed up with fake accounts, listed fake products and defrauded a lot of users. The fix was obvious: verify people. But fast listing was the product, and most of Kusnap’s users are local shop owners who aren’t very tech-savvy. The whole idea had been to spare them the hassle of a verification flow.

items: My part

As Head of Design I worked across the whole product. For the two features here, I designed the verification and listing flows on web, and supervised the mobile app versions, which another designer built.
Constraints
Listing had to stay fast, because speed is the product. Every step had to be simple enough for a shop owner to finish without help.

blocks.v: Anyone could sign up and list in seconds, with no checks at all. Fraudsters used that to open fake accounts, list fake products and take buyers’ money, and support tickets piled up. Honest sellers paid for it too: buyers started assuming anyone could be a scammer.
The goal
Make buyers and sellers trust each other, without slowing down listing or losing shop owners who aren’t comfortable with tech.

sections.title: Listening to buyers, sellers and support

notes.p: Poor support after a sale, when issues come up

blocks.v: I interviewed buyers and sellers, reviewed support tickets and spoke with business owners about where trust broke down.
Why Kusnap needed verification

after.v: What it meant for the design

items: Buyers fear scams and unreliable sellers
BVN or NIN ties every verified seller to a real, traceable person
Buyers fear fake listings
Specification fields that fit the category, and a listing-quality meter, so listings show real detail
Sellers find it hard to build trust and look credible
A verified tick buyers can see on the seller card and profile
Sellers lose sales when buyers hesitate
The tick answers “is this seller real?” before anyone pays

blocks.v: Before paying, a buyer asks two things: who am I buying from, and is this item what it says? Verification answers the first. Better listings answer the second: a Listing Quality meter on the seller’s side shows how complete a listing is and nudges sellers to add the details buyers need to decide with confidence. Three principles guided both: simple, so it’s quick; visible, so trust shows; scalable, so it grows with the user base.

items.t: Verify in two steps, phone first
items.why: A one-time code takes seconds and stops throwaway accounts. The ID step adds real trust when someone is ready.
items.cost: For a short window an account is phone-verified only, so the badge shows each step separately.

items.t: Earn a badge, don’t block sign-up
items.yes: Open sign-up, with unlocks for the verified
items.why: Sign-up stays fast. Verified sellers get a visible badge, and product uploads unlock after verifying.
items.cost: Unverified accounts still exist, so the badge has to be clear enough for buyers to choose verified sellers.

items.yes: Let people enter their BVN or NIN
items.why: Both are government-verifiable, unique to one person and linked to the holder’s bank account, so one number can’t back two sellers. Offering either means people can verify with whichever they have.
items.cost: Two ID checks to connect and maintain instead of one.

items.no: Ask for every detail on every listing
items.yes: Quick list from a past listing
items.why: Many sellers restock the same items. Reusing a sold-out listing fills the form in one tap.
items.cost: Old details can be out of date, so every field stays editable and the preview shows the result before posting.

items.why: A live score and preview show sellers what buyers will see, and nudge them toward 80% without stopping them posting.
items.cost: Some listings still go live below 80%.

blocks.v: A one-time code confirms the phone. Then an ID number confirms the person: people choose either their Bank Verification Number (BVN) or their National Identification Number (NIN), and enter their name as it appears on it. Both are government-verifiable, no two people share a number, and both are linked to the holder’s bank account, so a verified seller is tied to a real, traceable person. Verified sellers get a tick everyone can see, and product uploads unlock.

blocks.cap: The verification flow. It plays on its own; click inside to take over.
Where buyers see it: the verified tick on the seller card, on desktop and on mobile.
blocks.title: The verified tick on the seller card, on the desktop product page, then the same page reshaping into mobile

blocks.v: Shops get verified too
Business owners start from their dashboard. Under Manage › Shops, a single prompt invites them to verify their store, so a shop can show buyers it is the real thing.

blocks.cap: Store verification starts from the seller dashboard, then checks the shop is ready.
blocks.title: Store verification from the seller dashboard: Get Verified Now opens the verification intro, Start Application opens the eligibility check

blocks.v: Verification added a step, so listing had to give sellers their speed back. I rebuilt Add New Product as two short steps, with a live preview and a listing-quality meter that turns from red to gold to green as the listing improves.

blocks.cap: Listing a new product from scratch. It plays on its own; click inside to take over.

blocks.v: Reuse what you’ve sold before
Quick List shows a seller’s out-of-stock listings. One tap fills the name, category, photos and price, and every field stays editable.

blocks.cap: Pick a past listing and its details fill the new product form.
blocks.title: Quick List opens, a past listing is picked, and its name, category, price and photos fill the Add New Product form

blocks.v: Details that fit, delivery set once

Sellers only see the specification fields that fit what they’re selling: a phone asks for storage, RAM and battery, while shoes ask for size and material. Every phone listing then shows the same set of details, so buyers can compare two phones side by side. Delivery works the same way, set once: the seller enters one fee for buyers in their city and one for buyers elsewhere, ticks “Save as default”, and every product they list carries those fees from then on. The default is a starting point: a seller can still set a different delivery price on any single product, say for something bulky.

blocks.cap: Specifications that follow the category, and a default delivery cost that every product starts with.
blocks.title: Specifications fill in for a phone, then swap to shoe fields when the category changes; delivery costs are set once, saved as default, and appear on every product

after.v: Beyond the numbers, the marketing team reported more products being listed and more engagement across the platform after the verification and listing updates shipped.

A badge tells buyers who they are dealing with before any money moves.
Step one: a one-time code confirms the phone number.
Step two: a government-issued ID confirms the person.
Business-owned stores get their own check, on the web too.
exp: A one-time code for the phone, then a government-issued ID. Verified buyers and sellers get a badge everyone can see.
Business-owned stores go through their own check, so a shop can show buyers it is the real thing.

cases.title: Bulvds
cases.headline:
A wallet that makes
short-let payments trustworthy
cases.blurb: Bulvds makes short-let and rental stays simple for everyone: explorers looking for a place, managers who run listings, and homeowners who own them. Money was where trust broke down, so I designed the Bulvds Wallet: one place to fund bookings, get refunds, receive payouts and see exactly where every naira is.
story: Money you can see, from booking to payout
Managers weren’t sure when they’d be paid, renters worried about getting deposits back, and payments often happened off the platform.
The Bulvds Wallet puts payments, refunds and commissions in one place, with balances that say exactly what is ready, what is coming and what has gone.

blocks.v: Bulvds redefines modern living by simplifying short-let and rental experiences. It serves three kinds of people: explorers (renters) looking for a stay, managers (agents) running listings, and homeowners overseeing their spaces.

The platform brings discovering, booking and managing properties into one place, built on transparency, trust and convenience. Every one of those journeys ends in money changing hands, and that is where the experience fell short.

items: Explorers
Renters who discover, book and pay for stays, and wait for their caution fee to come back.
Managers
Agents who list properties, take bookings and earn commissions.
Homeowners
Owners who oversee their spaces and get paid for them.

blocks.v: Users faced real friction managing payments. Managers were frustrated by unclear payout timelines, while renters worried about getting their caution fee back. International users were blocked by limited payment options. Together, these led to a lack of trust, frequent disputes and a fragmented experience that stopped people rebooking inside the app.
The goal
Design a wallet that delivers clarity, trust and accessibility, by making transactions transparent, refunds predictable and payments inclusive for local and international users.

notes.p: Managers don’t know when they’ll get paid, so cash flow is unpredictable.
Renters are anxious about when they’ll get their security deposit back.
Without transparency, disputes are nearly impossible to resolve, and confidence erodes.
Paying means leaving the app, so rebooking feels disconnected.
International guests can’t book without payment options that work for them.

blocks.v: Five pain points came up across renters, managers and international guests.

after.v: What it meant for the design

items: Managers can’t predict payouts
A withdrawal balance that shows what’s ready to cash out, and incoming funds that show what’s on the way
Renters worry about their deposit
Refunds show as incoming funds, with a notification when they land
Disputes are hard to resolve
A full transaction history with clear receipts and escrow notes
Paying means leaving the app
Fund the wallet, pay for bookings and withdraw without leaving Bulvds
International guests can’t pay
Top up by card, bank transfer or cryptocurrency

blocks.v: Four principles shaped every screen of the wallet.

items: Transparency first
Clear wallet breakdowns (total, withdrawal and incoming funds), with a short explanation for every balance.
Seamless flows
Fund the wallet and withdraw inside the app, so people don’t depend on outside payment systems.
Inclusive by default
Several ways to fund the wallet, so everyone can book without friction, at home or abroad.
Built for trust
Real-time notifications, a detailed transaction history and an easy way to raise a dispute.

blocks.v: The Bulvds Wallet handles payments, refunds and commissions in one place. It replaces the guesswork with three balances anyone can read at a glance.

items: Total balance
All the funds in the wallet.
Withdrawal balance
Funds that are ready to cash out.
Incoming funds
Payments or refunds that are pending and will be credited soon.

blocks.cap: The wallet home: three balances, and a plain explanation for each.
blocks.title: The wallet home, then View Breakdown opens the wallet overview and an explanation of each balance

blocks.v: Fund it any way you like
Users top up the wallet with Paystack (card, USSD or bank transfer) or with cryptocurrency. International guests can book without a local bank card, and everyone can pre-fund before checkout.

blocks.cap: Top up with Paystack or crypto: USDT converts to Naira as you type, and the new balance shows straight away.
blocks.title: Fund wallet, choose crypto, enter an amount in USDT, see the Naira value, confirm, and the balance updates

blocks.v: Cash out in a few taps
Agents and renters withdraw straight to their bank account. The withdrawal balance shows exactly what can go out today, so nobody is surprised by what can’t.

blocks.cap: Withdraw to a saved bank account, confirmed with a 4-digit code.
blocks.title: Withdraw, choose bank transfer, enter the amount and a note, confirm with a code, funds sent

blocks.v: Pay for a stay your way

At checkout, renters can add extras like a chef, a driver or a PS5, then choose how to pay: from the Bulvds Wallet, with Paystack by card or bank transfer, or with Split Payment, which uses the wallet balance and pays the rest with Paystack. Paying from the wallet keeps the whole booking inside the app.

blocks.cap: Add extras, then pay from the wallet, with Paystack, or split between the two.
blocks.title: Review the booking, add a PS5 as an extra, open the payment summary, compare payment methods and pay from the wallet

blocks.v: See where your money is
A full history of every transaction, from payments and commissions to refunds and withdrawals. Each one opens a clear receipt, and escrow notes explain any money that is being held and why.

blocks.cap: Every transaction, with a receipt for each, and a clear failed state.
blocks.title: Recent transactions, then a caution fee refund and a failed withdrawal opened as receipts

sections.title: A way in for renters and hosts

blocks.v: I also redesigned onboarding. Three slides speak to the people Bulvds serves: finding a verified space, getting a feel for the lifestyle around it, and managing properties. Each one carries an isometric illustration I made for the app.

Sign-up starts with just an email. Bulvds checks whether an account already exists and, if not, goes straight to creating one, so nobody has to choose between “log in” and “sign up” before they’ve started. Once the account is made, people land on their feed.

blocks.cap: Splash, three slides with the isometric illustrations, sign-up by email, then the feed.
blocks.title: The splash screen, three onboarding slides with isometric illustrations, the welcome screen, an email that is new to Bulvds leading to Create your account, then the home feed scrolling

blocks.v: Hosts get their own path
Agents, landlords and property managers tap Continue as Host. A short page explains what listing on Bulvds gives them before they create a host account.

sections.title: Tested with the people who use it

blocks.v: Before the wallet and the new onboarding shipped, we ran usability tests with existing Bulvds users: renters, agents and homeowners who already book and list on the app. They worked through the same journeys shown above.

items: Reading the wallet
The three balances, and what each one means.
Money in and out
Funding the wallet, then withdrawing to a bank account.
Paying for a stay
Checkout with extras, paying from the wallet, with Paystack or split between the two.
Getting started
Onboarding, and signing up with just an email.

blocks.v: The feedback came back positive. Users found the wallet clear and the flows easy to follow, which gave the team the confidence to build it as designed.

cases.statement: When people can see their money, they stop worrying about it.
shots: Payments, refunds and commissions in one wallet.
Total balance, what is ready to withdraw and what is still coming.
Top up by card, bank transfer or crypto.
Cash out to a bank account in a couple of taps.
Paying for a booking straight from the wallet.
exp: Fund the wallet by card, bank transfer or crypto, so local and international guests can both pay.
Agents and renters cash out to a bank account. Balances say what is ready, what is coming and what has gone.
cases.problem: Managers couldn’t predict payouts, renters worried about getting their caution fee back, and international guests were blocked by limited payment options.
cases.goal: A wallet that delivers clarity, trust and accessibility: transparent transactions, predictable refunds and payments that work for local and international users.

glance.problem: Managers couldn’t predict payouts, renters worried about deposits, and international guests couldn’t pay at all.
glance.did: Designed the wallet: balances, multi-source funding, withdrawals and a full transaction history, plus a new onboarding flow.
glance.result: Usability tests with existing Bulvds users came back positive.

cases.title: ShareBuddy
cases.headline:
Splitting the bill
without the awkward bit
cases.blurb: Social bill-splitting and group wallets for young Nigerians, so paying friends back takes one tap.
story: A group wallet with a friend in it
Splitting rent, trips and dinners in Lagos usually ends with screenshots, reminders and someone left out of pocket.
ShareBuddy gives a group one wallet, splits the bill and keeps track of who has paid. Buddy, the mascot, does the nudging so friends don’t have to.

p: A social bill-splitting and group wallet app for Nigerians aged 18 to 35, starting in Lagos.

list: Naira wallets for groups, powered by Paystack.
Stablecoins as a way to fund the wallet, which stays in naira.

p: A bright red, #E8273A, and Buddy, a mascot who reminds people to pay so their friends don’t have to.

cases.statement: Money between friends should feel like a favour, not a debt.
shots: A bright red brand with a friend in it.
Split a bill between a group in one go.
Buddy does the nudging, so friends don’t have to.
One wallet for the whole group, in naira.
exp: Group wallets in naira, powered by Paystack.
Stablecoins as a way to fund the wallet, which stays in naira.
cases.problem: Splitting rent, trips and dinners between friends ends in screenshots, reminders and someone left out of pocket.
cases.goal: A group wallet that splits the bill and keeps track, so nobody has to chase anyone.

cases.title: Oghosa
cases.headline:
A brand that holds
many businesses
cases.blurb: Brand identity and strategy for a forward-looking investment and management company.
story: Oghosa Holdings invests in and manages many different businesses. The mark puts those units inside a bag: protected, held together, looked after.

p: Oghosa Holdings is a forward-looking investment and management company. I worked on its brand strategy and identity.
The company’s units sit inside a bag: a symbol of protecting and managing a range of businesses.
Very dark and dark greys, beige, golden sand and coffee brown, with a serif that carries credibility.
Contemporary and vibrant, with imagery borrowed from pop culture to balance credibility with creativity.
The identity across professional and lifestyle pieces.

cases.statement: Serious about money, never dull about it.
shots: An identity for an investment and management company.
Business units held inside a bag: protected, together.
Greys, beige, golden sand and coffee brown, with a serif.
exp: Very dark and dark greys, beige, golden sand and coffee brown.
A serif for credibility, with pop-culture imagery that keeps it lively.
cases.problem: A company that invests in and manages many different businesses needed one identity that felt credible without feeling dull.
cases.goal: A mark and a system that say protection and care, and still feel lively.

cases.title: Kauri
cases.headline:
Money that moves
between African cities
cases.blurb: A payments brand for small businesses and startups trading between African cities, starting with Lagos and Cairo.
story: Kauri is a respelling of cowrie, the shell that was traded as money across Africa for centuries. Said KOW-ree.
The brand is for small businesses and startups in Africa’s top and emerging cities that need to pay one another easily, starting with Lagos and Cairo.

p: A side project to stretch my brand and product design: a payments brand that makes it easy for African small businesses and startups to trade with one another across borders.
Kauri respells cowrie, the shell once traded as money across the continent. A name that carries trade in its history, and still reads as modern.

list: Small businesses and startups in top and emerging African cities.
Paying one another as easily as paying someone down the road.

cases.statement: The oldest money on the continent, for the newest businesses on it.
shots: Kauri: cowrie, the first money traded across Africa.
Paying across borders as easily as down the road.
exp: Small businesses and startups in Africa’s top and emerging cities.
Lets them pay one another across borders as easily as paying someone down the road.
cases.problem: Small businesses and startups want to trade with each other across African cities, and paying each other is the hard part.
cases.goal: A payments brand that feels trusted across borders and rooted in the continent, starting with Lagos and Cairo.
